title: Simple Perfect-Information Game
body_html:
Simple Perfect-Information Game

A two-player perfect-information game is simple if its terminal outcomes are partitioned into winning sets $(R_1,R_2)$, where reaching a terminal node in $R_i$ means player $i$ wins and the other player loses.

A winning strategy for player $i$ is a strategy $\sigma_i$ such that, for every opponent strategy $\sigma_{-i}$, $$ F(\sigma_i,\sigma_{-i})\in R_i. $$
